newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares ebb in average, mixed trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares ebb in average, mixed trade.

text.p: Share prices on the Cairo bourse were slightly lower on Monday in below average trade focused on a mixed bag of stocks in the banking, mills and cements sectors.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) index shied away from the previous day's level by 0.37 points to 370.79. Turnover was 52.51 million pounds ($15.46 million).
The three busiest shares fell, according to the CMA report.
"On the whole, the majority of the shares were either stagnant or slightly up. Volume is on the average," said Neveen al-Tahry of Delta EAB.
"There's a lot of demand but it's at lower prices. But there isn't that much offer. People tend to hold on because they think prices are going up."
Central and West Delta Flour Mills was the heaviest traded share of the day with 6.51 million pounds turnover. But its share price reversed direction, falling by 1.54 to close at 88 pounds.
Suez Cement was the second most popular share with 4.43 million pounds turnover. Its share also fell, closing 0.32 lower at 67.58 pounds.
"Most of the mills and the cements look extremely attractive," Tahry said.

But investors also dipped into the banking sector and brought Commercial International Bank into the top three stocks in terms of turnover. It finished down 1.5 at 75 pounds in 4.425 million pounds turnover.
Egyptian American Bank also found favour on the bourse and rose 6.84 pounds to close at 143.71 in 3.69 million pounds worth of trade.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 531.72 points from 529.86 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms fell to 267.77 from 268.68.
Out of the 86 shares traded, 26 ended up, 35 fell and 25 were unchanged.
